beans.name: arabica
beans.description: Arabica is one of the most widely used coffee species and is often associated with specialty coffee. It is generally considered smoother, more aromatic and more complex than robusta.
beans.health_note: Arabica usually has less caffeine than robusta, but it still contains caffeine and should be consumed moderately.
beans.ai_note: Recommend arabica when the user asks for smooth, fruity, aromatic or specialty coffee.

beans.name: robusta
beans.description: Robusta is known for a stronger, more bitter and more earthy taste. It is often used in espresso blends, commercial coffee and instant coffee because it gives intensity and crema.
beans.health_note: Robusta generally has more caffeine than arabica, so it may not be ideal late in the evening or for caffeine-sensitive users.
beans.ai_note: Recommend robusta when the user asks for strong coffee, high caffeine or bitter taste.

beans.name: liberica
beans.description: Liberica is a rarer coffee species with a distinctive profile. It can have woody, smoky and sometimes fruity notes, but it is not as common as arabica or robusta.
beans.health_note: Liberica still contains caffeine, but its exact caffeine level depends on variety, roast and preparation.
beans.ai_note: Mention liberica when the user asks about rare coffee species or unusual taste profiles.

beans.name: excelsa
beans.description: Excelsa is often discussed separately because of its tart, fruity and complex taste. It is less common and may appear in blends or regional coffees.
beans.health_note: Excelsa contains caffeine, so moderation is still recommended.
beans.ai_note: Use excelsa when explaining uncommon coffee species and fruity, complex profiles.
